newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bond yields were nudged lower in Wednesday's afternoon session on the back of offshore interest and gains on the U.S. T-bond, traders said.
The benchmark R150's yield ticked down to 14.255 percent after hitting a high of 14.325 percent earlier in the day, compared to 14.265 percent late on Tuesday.

"The market wants to go somewhere because it's been in a very small range. I think it's a pressure cooker and I think it's going to break on the down side," one trader said. "We've been waiting for something to get it moving."

U.S. Treasury prices peaked with the 30-year yield at 6.50 percent -- its lowest since December 10, 1996, after the release of benign June retail inflation which was up just 0.1 percent against May's 0.2 percent
Another trader said although there were no substantial trades on the South African bonds market on Wednesday, a bullish mood could return to the market in the short term.

"We've been in a consolidation with a bit of cutting out of jobbers' long positions and giving institutions time to get their strategy right for the year. I think we will see local institutions buying next week," he added.
On a quiet currency market, the rand was last at 4.5530/60 against the dollar from 4.5545/75 late on Tuesday.

Dealers said the rand was stuck in the 4.55 to 4.56 range as the central bank was again seen capping the local unit. Some local and foreign interest was seen on the day but it was evenly matched. A sideways move was also expected for Thursday.
"It's being capped topside around 4.56 so we're stuck. Guys aren't doing all that much because know have a cap on the topside at the moment so why bother," said one dealer.
"Nothing happened, it's been a lacklustre day," said another.

On the crosses the rand was last pegged at 0.3949/3054 marks from 0.3948/3953 marks on Tuesday, and at 7.6236/6332 on sterling from 7.6016/6112 previously. Against the yen the local unit was quoted at 25.4967/5354 from 25.2979/3366 on Tuesday.
Foreigners were net sellers of South African bonds worth 480.54 million rand on Tuesday, after selling 330.49 million rand on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
The total value of Tuesday's Bond Exchange turnover more than doubled to 9.4 billion rand from 3.99 billion rand on Monday.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 8.496 billion rand on Tuesday from 7.757 billion rand on Monday.
